items.title: Coffee Meets Room
items.question: A hot coffee cools in a room while the combined coffee-room energy stays constant. The total entropy can still rise because that energy becomes spread across more molecular motions.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Energy conservation fixes the total amount, while entropy tracks how broadly that energy is distributed among accessible microscopic states.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. Cooling does not destroy the coffee's energy; heat enters the room and becomes less concentrated, increasing the number of ways the combined energy can be arranged.
items.lessonContent: Energy conservation and entropy growth describe different features of a process.

items.title: Fridge Exception
items.question: Because a refrigerator makes its interior colder and more organized, it lowers the total entropy of the kitchen plus refrigerator while running.
items.correctExplanation: Right. The refrigerator exports heat and adds electrical work that ultimately warms the kitchen, producing more entropy outside than it removes inside.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. A refrigerator can reduce entropy in its cold compartment only by consuming work and dumping a larger heat load into the room, so the combined entropy rises.
items.lessonContent: A subsystem may lose entropy when an external device pumps energy away from it.

items.title: Expansion Without Cooling
items.question: An ideal gas freely expands into an evacuated chamber without doing work or exchanging heat. Its entropy rises even though its internal energy and temperature remain unchanged.
items.correctExplanation: Exactly. The molecules gain access to more positions, increasing the number of compatible microstates without changing an ideal gas's kinetic-energy distribution.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. In free expansion, no heat enters and no boundary work leaves; for an ideal gas the temperature stays fixed, but the energy-bearing molecules can occupy a larger volume, so entropy increases.
items.lessonContent: Entropy can increase by spreading matter and its energy over more spatial states.

items.title: Temperature Verdict
items.question: If a system's temperature does not change, its entropy cannot change either.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Isothermal expansion, mixing, and phase changes can alter the number of accessible states while temperature remains fixed.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Temperature characterizes an energy distribution, but entropy also depends on accessible volume, particle arrangements, and phase, so equal temperature does not guarantee equal entropy.
items.lessonContent: Temperature and entropy are related state variables but they are not interchangeable.

items.title: Identical Reunion
items.question: Removing a partition between equal samples of the same gas at the same temperature and pressure creates the same mixing-entropy increase as mixing two different gases.
items.correctExplanation: Right. Identical particles do not acquire a new physically distinguishable label when the divider is removed, avoiding the fictitious entropy jump known from the Gibbs paradox.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Mixing distinguishable gases opens new composition arrangements, but exchanging identical particles across an imaginary boundary creates no new observable macrostate and no corresponding mixing entropy.
items.lessonContent: Entropy counts physically distinguishable possibilities rather than labels invented by an observer.

items.title: Two Gases Mix
items.question: When equal-temperature samples of two different ideal gases mix in an insulated container, entropy can rise without any net energy entering because each species spreads through more volume.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. The total energy can remain fixed while each distinguishable species gains many more accessible positional arrangements.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. No heat supply is required: mixing disperses the existing molecular energy and species labels over a larger set of accessible microstates.
items.lessonContent: An entropy increase need not be caused by adding energy to a system.

items.title: Disorder Definition
items.question: Thermodynamic entropy is scientifically defined as the visible messiness or disorder of an object.
items.correctExplanation: Exactly. Entropy has quantitative definitions based on energy dispersal, state probabilities, and accessible microstates; visual untidiness is only an unreliable analogy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. A messy desk is not assigned thermodynamic entropy by appearance. Entropy quantifies how energy and probability are distributed across microscopic states consistent with macroscopic constraints.
items.lessonContent: Disorder is a metaphor, not the operational definition of thermodynamic entropy.

items.title: Melting Ledger
items.question: At the melting point, ice can absorb energy and become liquid water without warming; its entropy increases because the energy occupies more accessible molecular states.
items.correctExplanation: Right. Latent heat changes the phase rather than the temperature, opening many more molecular arrangements and increasing entropy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. During melting, added energy breaks down the constraints of the crystal structure instead of raising temperature, so the liquid supports more accessible ways to distribute that energy.
items.lessonContent: During a phase transition, energy can change molecular constraints without changing temperature.

items.title: Freezing Pays Out
items.question: When water freezes in a cold room, the water's entropy falls, but the combined water-room entropy can rise because released heat spreads into the surroundings.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. The forming crystal narrows water's accessible states, while heat released to colder surroundings produces a larger compensating entropy increase.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. Freezing lowers the subsystem's entropy, but the latent heat does not vanish; dispersing it into the colder environment raises surrounding entropy enough to satisfy the second law.
items.lessonContent: Phase formation can concentrate matter into fewer microscopic arrangements locally.

items.title: Uphill Heat
items.question: Heat naturally flowing from a colder object to a hotter one would spread energy more evenly and therefore increase total entropy.
items.correctExplanation: Right. Cold-to-hot transfer concentrates energy further; without compensating work or another change, it decreases total entropy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Moving heat into the hotter body steepens the temperature imbalance rather than flattening it, so such transfer requires work, as in a refrigerator.
items.lessonContent: Spontaneous heat flow reduces temperature differences and spreads energy more evenly.

items.title: Work Equals Heat
items.question: Transferring 100 joules as organized mechanical work has exactly the same entropy transfer as delivering 100 joules as heat at any temperature.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Work transfers energy without carrying thermodynamic entropy in the heat-transfer sense, while reversible heat transfer carries entropy Q/T.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Joules count energy amount, not dispersal quality. Mechanical work is directed energy, whereas heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference and carries entropy proportional to Q/T.
items.lessonContent: Heat and work are two modes of energy transfer, not substances stored in an object.

items.title: Equilibrium Peak
items.question: For an isolated system with fixed total energy and constraints, thermal equilibrium is the macrostate compatible with overwhelmingly many microstates and thus maximum entropy.
items.correctExplanation: Exactly. Equilibrium dominates because there are vastly more microscopic ways for energy to be broadly distributed than concentrated in a special region.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. Maximum entropy does not mean maximum energy; energy is already fixed. It means the fixed energy is distributed among the greatest accessible set of microscopic arrangements.
items.lessonContent: Equilibrium is a statistical statement about the most numerous compatible microscopic arrangements.

items.title: Counting Possibilities
items.question: If one macrostate corresponds to a million accessible microstates and another to only a hundred at the same energy, the first has higher Boltzmann entropy.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Boltzmann's relation S = k ln W assigns greater entropy to the macrostate with more compatible microstates.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. Entropy grows with the logarithm of multiplicity, so a macrostate compatible with more microscopic arrangements has higher entropy under the same constraints.
items.lessonContent: A macrostate specifies coarse properties such as energy, volume, and particle number.

items.title: Double the Sample
items.question: Combining two independent identical samples doubles their energy but leaves their entropy unchanged because temperature stays the same.
items.correctExplanation: Right. Entropy is extensive: doubling the amount of an independent material at the same intensive conditions approximately doubles its entropy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Temperature is intensive and can stay fixed as sample size changes, while both energy and entropy scale with the amount of material.
items.lessonContent: Extensive quantities scale with system size; energy, volume, particle number, and entropy are examples.

items.title: Law Without Exceptions
items.question: The second law forbids even a momentary entropy decrease in every tiny subsystem, so molecular-scale fluctuations toward greater energy concentration are impossible.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. The second law is statistical; small systems can fluctuate toward lower entropy briefly, while large uncompensated decreases are fantastically improbable.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Random molecular motion permits temporary local concentration, especially at small scales. The law describes the overwhelmingly probable trend and the nondecrease of appropriate averages or total accounting.
items.lessonContent: The second law emerges from probability over enormous numbers of microscopic degrees of freedom.

items.title: Life's Loophole
items.question: Living organisms violate the second law by building highly organized structures from simpler nutrients.
items.correctExplanation: Exactly. Organisms are open systems that maintain local structure by taking in concentrated energy and exporting heat and waste, increasing total entropy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Biological organization is paid for by metabolism: useful energy enters, while more dispersed thermal energy and waste leave, so organism plus environment obeys the second law.
items.lessonContent: The second law does not require every open subsystem to become less structured.

items.title: Radiant Spread
items.question: When concentrated sunlight is absorbed by Earth and later emitted as many lower-energy infrared photons, energy is conserved while entropy increases.
items.correctExplanation: Right. Roughly the same energy leaves, but it is distributed among more lower-energy photons and directions, providing the entropy export that supports local processes on Earth.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. Earth does not merely return identical sunlight; it degrades concentrated high-temperature radiation into more dispersed low-temperature infrared radiation with greater entropy.
items.lessonContent: Radiation carries both energy and entropy.

items.title: Insulated Means Fixed
items.question: Any adiabatic process has constant entropy because no heat crosses the system boundary.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Reversible adiabatic processes are isentropic, but irreversible adiabatic processes such as free expansion generate entropy internally.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Adiabatic means no heat transfer, not no entropy production. Friction, mixing, or free expansion can spread energy internally and raise entropy inside an insulated system.
items.lessonContent: Adiabatic describes a boundary condition: no energy crosses as heat.

items.title: Open-System Balance
items.question: If entropy inside an open system decreases, entropy must have been destroyed there in violation of thermodynamics.
items.correctExplanation: Right. Entropy can leave with heat or matter; the balance requires entropy generation to be nonnegative, not the stored entropy of every open system to increase.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. An open system can export entropy faster than it generates it, lowering its own stored entropy while the wider system's total still rises.
items.lessonContent: An entropy balance separates storage, transfer across boundaries, and internal generation.

items.title: Battery Afterglow
items.question: When a battery discharges through a resistor, its stored energy is annihilated and replaced by newly created heat, which is why entropy rises.
items.correctExplanation: Exactly. The energy is conserved: concentrated chemical free energy becomes broadly distributed thermal energy, and that degradation raises entropy.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. No energy is annihilated or created. The battery's organized chemical potential becomes electrical work and then dispersed molecular motion in the resistor and surroundings.
items.lessonContent: A battery stores energy in chemical gradients capable of driving directed electrical work.

items.title: Useful Energy Lost
items.question: When entropy is produced in an isolated process, some energy is destroyed, so the final total energy is smaller.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Total energy is conserved; what falls is exergy, the portion that could produce work relative to the environment.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Entropy production spreads energy into less exploitable forms without reducing its amount. The lost quantity is work potential, not energy itself.
items.lessonContent: The first law conserves energy while the second law limits its usefulness.

items.title: Cold Receives More
items.question: For the same small reversible heat input Q, a colder body receives a larger entropy increase than a hotter body because the change is approximately Q/T.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Dividing the same energy transfer by a lower absolute temperature gives a larger entropy change.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is True. Entropy measures dispersal relative to the existing thermal scale, so a joule transferred reversibly at lower kelvin carries more entropy than a joule at higher kelvin.
items.lessonContent: For reversible heat transfer, the entropy increment is energy divided by absolute temperature.

items.title: Engine's Full Take
items.question: A cyclic heat engine can convert all heat drawn from a single reservoir into work because work contains less entropy than heat.
items.correctExplanation: Right. A cyclic engine must reject some heat and entropy to a colder sink; complete conversion from one reservoir would leave nowhere for the incoming entropy to go.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Work can leave without carrying the heat reservoir's entropy, so a cyclic engine needs a cold sink to accept that entropy along with rejected energy.
items.lessonContent: Heat engines convert part of an energy flow down a temperature gradient into work.

items.title: Entropy's Unit
items.question: Because entropy concerns energy spreading, it is measured in joules, exactly like energy itself.
items.correctExplanation: Exactly. Thermodynamic entropy is measured in joules per kelvin; microscopic entropy uses Boltzmann's constant to supply those units.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Entropy is not another pile of energy. Its unit is joules per kelvin, consistent with the relation dS = reversible heat divided by absolute temperature.
items.lessonContent: Units distinguish entropy from the energy whose distribution it describes.

items.title: Information Reset
items.question: Erasing a memory bit can be performed with no thermodynamic consequence because information is abstract rather than physical.
items.correctExplanation: Correct. Logically irreversible reset compresses two possible logical states into one and must export at least kT ln 2 of heat per bit in the ideal limit.
items.incorrectExplanation: It is False. Memory is represented by physical states. Resetting an unknown bit removes a distinction and requires compensating entropy to be released to the environment, as captured by Landauer's principle.
items.lessonContent: Information must be encoded in physical degrees of freedom such as charge or magnetization.
